title: bug: a symlinked spelling of --project reads a live native daemon.json as 'projectPath mismatch' and deletes it without a /health probe
description: path.resolve is lexical. With a healthy daemon recorded under P, existingDaemonBlocksStart(<symlink to P>) in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts returns false, deletes daemon.json without probing and lets a second daemon start over the same .moe/. Windows 8.3 short names and trailing-dot spellings behave the same. Scratch-probe repro on HEAD 933fc324 plus task-25ba449a: canonical gives blocks=true, probes=1, kept; symlink gives blocks=false, probes still 1, daemon.json deleted. This is pre-existing: the pre-task key also resolved lexically, and task-25ba449a covers only lexical aliases (//x, /x). A likely fix is to never delete a native 'projectPath mismatch' file whose pid is alive and whose /health answers with the recorded path and pid.

Add a nested `describe('on-disk aliases of --project')` at the end of `describe('native aliases of --project')`. Number its tests after the highest X already in the file (X16-X18 if c83d7847's X15 has landed).

Fixture:
- beforeEach: set `link = testDir + '-link'` and run `fs.symlinkSync(testDir, link, 'junction')`. A junction needs no admin rights on Windows, and POSIX ignores the type.
- Then assert that `[isSameProjectPath(link, testDir), fs.realpathSync.native(link) === fs.realpathSync.native(testDir)]` equals `[false, true]`.
- afterEach: `fs.unlinkSync` every link this block created, then remove each `other` dir with `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true })`. Never rmSync recursively through a link or junction. The outer afterEach still removes testDir.
- Give writeDaemonFiles an optional third parameter, `projectPath = testDir`, and use it for both daemon.json and the lock. Existing callers do not change.

X16 mirrors X12. Write its body once, as a local `async function blocksAndStops(recorded, caller)`:
- Start healthServer(recorded) with a request counter, call writeDaemonFiles(port, process.pid, recorded), and save `kept = files()`.
- Expect `[await existingDaemonBlocksStart(caller), probes, ...files()]` toEqual `[true, 1, ...kept]`.
- statusDaemon(caller) logs exactly `[{ status: 'running', owner: 'local', pid: process.pid }]`.
- With killSpyWithoutSignals, stopDaemon(caller) sends exactly `[[process.pid, 'SIGTERM']]`.
- Finally `[probes, ...files(), fs.existsSync(stopPath())]` toEqual `[3, ...kept, true]`.

X16 rows:
- Through it.each: [testDir, link] and [link, testDir].
- An 8.3 row as a separate `it.runIf(process.platform === 'win32')`, because it.each passes no test context:
  - Get `short` from `execSync('for %I in ("' + testDir + '") do @echo %~sI', { encoding: 'utf8', shell: 'cmd.exe', windowsHide: true }).trim()`.
  - Call `ctx.skip()` when testDir contains `"` or `%`, or when `short === testDir` (the volume has no 8.3 names).
  - Otherwise run blocksAndStops(testDir, short).

X17 mirrors X14, through it.each with [[testDir, link], [link, testDir]]:
- Set `owner = await lockOwner(ownerSpelling)`.
- Expect the lock's pid to equal owner.pid, and `fs.realpathSync.native(recorded.projectPath) === fs.realpathSync.native(testDir)`.
- `acquireLock(contender)` is false; the lock bytes are unchanged; the owner is alive with exitCode null.
- Timeout 60_000.

X18 is the control, through it.each(['directory', 'link to it']):
- Create `other = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'moe-daemon-other-'))`. `recorded` is `other` itself, or a second link that points at it.
- Start healthServer(recorded) with a counter and call writeDaemonFiles(port, process.pid, recorded).
- Expect `[await existingDaemonBlocksStart(testDir), probes, fs.existsSync(jsonPath()), fs.existsSync(lockPath())]` toEqual `[false, 0, false, false]`. A .moe copied from another live project is still cleaned up.

Also update the comment above `describe('native aliases of --project')`. Recorded and reported paths are compared as written, except that a native one may also name testDir on disk (symlink, junction, 8.3). Leave X1-X15 unchanged. Import execSync next to spawn.

Error handling in the tests:
- Failures must surface. No try/catch around assertions or fs calls.
- Cleanup does not use force: a missing link or dir throws.

approvedScope: New private helper namesOwnProject(recorded, own) in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts. It is not exported.

Its four call sites: the mismatch check in staleLockReason, the precheck in validateDaemonInfoForProject, and the metadata precheck and /health body check in probeDaemonHealth, plus their one-line why-comments.

packages/moe-daemon/src/index.test.ts: a nested describe inside 'native aliases of --project' holding X16-X18; an optional projectPath parameter on writeDaemonFiles; link and 8.3 fixture helpers; an execSync import; and the refreshed block comment.
reuse: Reuses isSameProjectPath for the final comparison and isForeignDaemonInfo for the side check. The tests reuse X12/X14's healthServer, writeDaemonFiles, files(), lockOwner and killSpyWithoutSignals.

fs.realpathSync.native rather than stat dev+ino: on Windows, ino is the 64-bit file index, which ReFS (Dev Drive) does not guarantee to be unique. A false 'same' could SIGTERM another project's daemon. A realpath failure only falls back to today's behavior.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts staleLockReason returns early for a foreign lock, then checks isSameProjectPath(info.projectPath, canonicalProjectPath(projectPath)) (landed in aeeca045).

validateDaemonInfoForProject computes own = canonicalProjectPath(projectPath) and checks isSameProjectPath(info.projectPath, own). probeDaemonHealth computes own = canonicalProjectPath(expectedProjectPath) and compares both info.projectPath and the /health body's projectPath with it. task-f0abb6d6 makes the probe async (healthProbeAddress) and keeps both comparisons.
The daemon writes the raw --project into daemon.json and reports it from /health. acquireLock writes canonicalProjectPath(projectPath). So a symlink spelling can sit on either side.

In index.test.ts, the 'native aliases of --project' block holds lockOwner, stopChild, files() and spelling(). Its parent 'daemon.json across the WSL boundary' holds writeDaemonFiles(port, pid), jsonPath, lockPath, stopPath and killSpyWithoutSignals. c83d7847 adds X15 after X14.

Planner probe, Node 24.16 on win32: junction and 8.3 spellings share dev:ino, and fs.realpathSync.native expands both to the long path. fs.realpathSync('C:\\PROGRA~1') stays unexpanded. '<dir>.' is ENOENT, so a trailing-dot spelling cannot read daemon.json. cmd's `for %I in ("<dir>") do @echo %~sI` prints the short path. Node 24.21 on Linux: realpathSync.native('//tmp/x') is '/tmp/x', which is why the helper needs the foreign guard.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
task-25ba449a rev2 set the rule this extends (mem:gotcha-native-lifecycle-versus-transport-path-identity): resolve only OUR side, and compare recorded and reported paths as written, because foreign data must never go through this host's resolver. This plan keeps that rule for foreign paths and adds an on-disk check only for native ones.

The transport key (comparableProjectPath) is a cross-package contract, pinned by scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs against the proxy dist. Do not touch it.

isSameProjectPath has exactly four lifecycle call sites, at lines 227, 323, 351 and 382 of aeeca045's index.ts.

CI runs daemon vitest only on ubuntu, so the worker's native-Windows leg is the only run of the win32 rows.

Lane order:
- index.ts: 25ba449a → f0abb6d6 → this task → 4ca62c89.
- index.test.ts: c83d7847 (tests only, adds X15) → this task. This task's dependsOn already lists all three predecessors.
planningNotes.risks:
- f0abb6d6 rewrites probeDaemonHealth (async, healthProbeAddress). Apply (c) and (d) to whatever shape it lands in.
- Windows junction cleanup must use unlinkSync, never a recursive rm. The planner probe confirmed that unlinkSync removes a junction.
- The 8.3 row skips on volumes without 8.3 names. That is fine elsewhere, but on this machine's C: temp it must run.
- realpath on an unreachable UNC server can stall for the SMB timeout. It only runs after a lexical mismatch, so this is accepted.
- Bind mounts stay a mismatch, as today, and are out of scope.
- Trailing-dot spellings are not a vector: Node prefixes win32 fs paths with \\?\, so `<dir>.` is ENOENT and nothing is read or deleted.
- If c83d7847's X15 has not landed when this starts, still number the new tests after the highest X in the file.
- The shared checkout's daemon node_modules is win32, so Linux runs need a snapshot (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
